candidates.attacker_control: The archive being extracted. In TarUnArchiver.execute() the entry name comes from TarArchiveEntry.getName() and the link target from te.getLinkName() (lines 112-114); in AbstractZipUnArchiver.execute() the name comes from the ZIP entry, including the attacker-controlled Unicode Path Extra Field (ZipEntryFileInfo.getName(), lines 86-102), and the symlink target from zf.getUnixSymlink(ze) (lines 204-215). Anyone who can make the application process a malicious ZIP/TAR (e.g. a dependency/JAR unpacked by a Maven plugin such as maven-assembly-plugin, or a user-supplied archive) controls these strings.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: 1) The only sanitizer is the external plexus-utils FileUtils.resolveFile (plexus-utils 3.1.0 per pom.xml); its source is not in this snapshot, so if it throws for canonicalized paths outside baseDir the '../' variant may be mitigated on some platforms - I could not verify this and no in-repo guarantee exists. 2) Overwrite semantics: default overwrite=true, and overwrite=false still allows creating new files outside the dir, so the guard does not close the issue. 3) File name from ZIP may be normalized by commons-compress? ZipArchiveEntry keeps the raw entry name; commons-compress is only used for reading, and TarArchiveEntry names are likewise used verbatim. 4) Tests: no traversal regression test or containment assertion exists in src/test (searches for '../', 'traversal', 'outside' found only symlink-destination expectations, e.g. PlexusIoZipFileResourceCollectionTest lines 94-101, which show outside-pointing symlink targets are accepted and returned unchanged). 5) Archive-creation paths (AbstractZipArchiver/TarArchiver) write entry names into archives, not to the filesystem, so they are not the same sink.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary file write/overwrite outside the intended extraction directory with attacker-controlled content, limited by the permissions of the process performing extraction (e.g. the build/agent user). Typical consequences: corruption or replacement of files the process can write (build outputs, config, scripts, startup/cron files) and creation of symlinks pointing anywhere the user can reference, which can lead to code execution or further file disclosure when later build/install steps follow them. Also makes extraction behave outside the caller-specified destination that many callers implicitly treat as a sandbox boundary.
candidates.prerequisites: Code that extracts an attacker-influenced ZIP/TAR into a directory using plexus-archiver's ZIP/TAR unarchivers (directly or through ArchiverManager/Maven plugins). The process must have write permission to the target location for the file-write vector; the symlink vector additionally needs a filesystem that permits symlink creation (POSIX) and entries ordered so the link precedes the write. overwrite=true (the default) is not required for creating new files outside the directory, and setOverwrite(false) only skips existing newer files. FileSelector filtering does not normalize or validate names.
candidates.root_cause: AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile(File,File,InputStream,String entryName,...,String symlinkDestination) uses the archive-supplied entry name directly to derive the output file (line 309: FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName)) and then opens it for write (line 338: new FileOutputStream(f)), and it passes the archive-supplied symlinkDestination straight to SymlinkUtils.createSymbolicLink(f, new File(symlinkDestination)) (line 327). The repository contains no check that the canonical target path is inside the destination directory and no check that a symlink target stays inside it; validation is wholly delegated to the external plexus-utils FileUtils.resolveFile (version 3.1.0 declared in pom.xml), whose containment behavior cannot be verified from this snapshot. Consequently entry names containing ../ (and, on POSIX, a symlink entry followed by a write through it) can escape the extraction directory.
candidates.title: Path traversal / arbitrary file write during archive extraction (entry name and symlink target are not constrained to the destination directory)
candidates.trace: TarUnArchiver.execute()/AbstractZipUnArchiver.execute() iterate archive entries -> extractFile(src, destDirectory, stream, entryName, ..., symlinkDestination) in AbstractUnArchiver -> line 309 derives File f from the raw entry name -> for a regular entry, line 338 opens new FileOutputStream(f) and copies attacker bytes into it; for a symlink entry, line 327 creates a link to an arbitrary target. No code in this repository compares f.getCanonicalPath()/getAbsolutePath() against dir (search for 'outside', 'normalize', 'getCanonical' finds no such check in the extraction path; only DirectoryArchiver/ResourceUtils use getCanonicalPath for equality). An entry named e.g. ../../<path> therefore causes a write outside dir, and a symlink entry (e.g. link -> /some/dir) followed by an entry under 'link/' redirects the write on platforms where canonicalization is not rejected by resolveFile. DirectoryArchiver.execute()/copyFile() (lines 86-99) contains the same pattern (destDirectory.getCanonicalPath() + File.separator + entry name, plus unvalidated symlink target) on a different call path.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed and not executed. The exact semantics of plexus-utils 3.1.0 FileUtils.resolveFile could not be inspected from this snapshot (dependency source absent), so whether the plain '../' vector is fully open in every deployment is uncertain; the unvalidated symlink-target creation and the absence of any in-repo containment check are directly visible in source. Binary test fixtures referenced by tests (jars/zips/tars) are not visible to read_file/search_code, and the repository history/patch metadata is not part of the snapshot, so I could not map this to a specific upstream advisory or confirm which exact release fixed it.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (Path Traversal); link-following/arbitrary symlink creation (CWE-59)

coverage_summary: Coverage: all 457 model-visible files were within scope; binary-like files are refused by read_file/skipped by search_code per the scope report, and one file was excluded by name/path, so the visible count is 457 of 458 root files. Main sources (140 Java files) were inspected, with focused review of extraction (AbstractUnArchiver, TarUnArchiver, AbstractZipUnArchiver, ZipUnArchiver, DirectoryArchiver), archive creation (AbstractZipArchiver, JarArchiver, Manifest, TarArchiver, War/Ear), compression/stream utilities, resource collections and all test classes/resources that are model-visible. The P1 relation index (1533 symbols, 2930 syntax edges, 3702 unresolved calls, no control/data-flow, partial index status) was used only for navigation; every cited edge/location was verified in source text. Coverage limitations: dependency sources (plexus-utils/plexus-io/commons-compress) and binary test fixtures are not in the snapshot, no tests/builds/scanners were executed, and jira/*.json (279 historical issue dumps) were treated as untrusted context and not exhaustively reviewed.
limitations: No runtime confirmation: no code, tests, or scanners were executed (as required), so the candidate is a source-evidence lead only.

plexus-utils 3.1.0 (and plexus-io 3.0.1, commons-compress 1.16.1) sources are external dependencies and not part of the snapshot; FileUtils.resolveFile's exact containment behavior could not be verified, which is the main uncertainty for the plain '../' vector.

Binary test fixtures referenced by visible tests (jars/zips/tars, e.g. src/test/jars/*.jar, symlinks.zip/symlinks.tar) are not visible to the tools, so related tests could not be read or reconstructed.

The P1 index has no data-flow/control-flow and unresolved calls (3702), so reachability of specific unarchiver instantiations from particular Maven plugins was reasoned about from the public class API and component metadata, not proven.
Repository history/patch metadata is absent, so the candidate could not be tied to a specific upstream fix commit or advisory (external services/ground truth were deliberately not consulted).
jira/*.json files are a large untrusted data dump and were only sampled; they were not treated as instructions or as proof of any vulnerability.

summary: Reviewed the plexus-archiver 3.6.0-SNAPSHOT source tree (457 model-visible files; 140 Java files parsed by the P1 index; jira/*.json are historical issue dumps, not code). The strongest source-supported issue is in the archive-extraction path: AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile() builds the output file directly from the archive entry name and writes through it (and creates symlinks from an unvalidated link destination) without any containment check that the result stays inside the destination directory. Both TarUnArchiver and AbstractZipUnArchiver feed attacker-controlled entry/link names into this sink, so a crafted ZIP/TAR can write files outside the intended extraction directory (classic "Zip Slip" / arbitrary file write). One candidate submitted; the missing symlink-target validation is part of the same root cause. No other issue in the repo reached the same evidence/impact bar.
